findings.title: Pagination total pages is off by one when count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit (for example 50 users with limit 50), this returns one extra page. The UI will show and allow navigation to a blank page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), and guard against limit <= 0.

findings.title: Member pagination can keep or request an offset beyond the last page
findings.body: findMembers clamps offset to user_count, but offset == user_count is past the last record; the maximum useful offset is user_count - limit. This can request an empty page, and after deleting the last member on a later page it can leave the UI stuck on an empty page. Clamp offset to Math.max(0, user_count - limit).

findings.title: Public members endpoint does not cap or validate limit
findings.body: members sets limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no lower or upper bound. A caller can pass a huge limit and force loading/serializing all group members, or pass 0/negative values causing empty responses, client-side division by zero, or SQL errors. Clamp limit to a positive maximum.

findings.title: Negative offset is accepted and can cause errors
findings.body: offset is taken directly as params[:offset].to_i. A negative offset is invalid for ActiveRecord/SQL and can result in a 500 error. Clamp offset to zero or greater.

findings.title: Group members JSON contract changed from array to object
findings.body: The members endpoint previously rendered a serialized array of users. It now returns an object with members and meta. Any existing API clients expecting an array will break. If this change is intentional, it should be documented or versioned; otherwise maintain backward compatibility.

findings.title: Admin group create/update payload changed incompatibly
findings.body: Create/update now expect flat params and no longer accept the previous nested group[...] payload or usernames during create/update. Existing API clients or plugins using the old contract will fail or silently ignore fields such as usernames and name. If intentional, provide documentation or a compatibility path.

findings.title: Group creation ignores alias_level
findings.body: The client sends alias_level when creating a group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. Any alias level selected while creating a group is silently dropped. Assign alias_level on create or remove the control for unsaved groups.

findings.title: Visible flag only accepts the literal string 'true'
findings.body: visible is set with params[:visible] == "true". JSON API clients sending boolean true, or values such as "1", will be treated as false, causing groups to be created or updated as hidden unexpectedly. Use proper boolean casting.

findings.title: add_members parsing is fragile and succeeds silently on invalid input
findings.body: add_members splits usernames on commas, does not strip whitespace, and silently ignores unknown usernames. Input like "bob, alice" or a typo can return success without adding the intended users. It also assumes a String; an array parameter would raise NoMethodError on split. Strip entries, validate usernames, and return errors for invalid input.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The test for refusing removal from automatic groups uses xhr :put, but the route is declared as DELETE and the successful removal test uses :delete. Controller specs bypass routing, so this does not verify the real endpoint verb.

findings.title: Save error handler assumes response is JSON with errors
findings.body: The failure handler does $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors. If the server responds with non-JSON output or a JSON body without errors, this throws and the user gets no feedback. Parse defensively and show a generic error message.
